title: PhilosophyPlatformGraph
description: Content contract for the comparative philosophy platform. Lifted from research Deliverable F.5 and extended. Every content file under /content is a *fragment*: an object carrying any subset of the top-level collections. Fragments are merged into one graph at build time. The verbatim F.5 seed instance is itself a valid fragment.

x-ontologyMapping.$comment: Research F.3. We do not publish RDF in the MVP, but the mapping is carried here so the store choice stays reversible (F.3, J.3).
x-ontologyMapping.upperOntology: CIDOC-CRM (ISO 21127) for historical entities; SKOS for the concept thesaurus and question taxonomy; schema.org for public-facing structured-data markup only.

Passage.crm: E73 Information Object (part of a Text via P148 has component)

Concept.skos: skos:Concept; prefLabel = source term, altLabel = transliteration + standard rendering

Question.skos: skos:Concept in the question scheme; domain = skos:broader

Equivalence.skos: convergenceType maps onto SKOS mapping relations: genuine -> skos:closeMatch (never exactMatch: no two positions from unconnected traditions are identical), superficial -> skos:relatedMatch, translation_artifact -> skos:relatedMatch with an explicit caution. We deliberately never emit skos:exactMatch.

HoldsRelation.crm: reified as E13 Attribute Assignment: P14 carried out by (the scholarship), P141 assigned (the Position), P140 assigned attribute to (the Thinker). This is what carries qualification and epistemicStatus.

$fragment.description: Human-readable provenance note for this file. Ignored by the loader.

Slug.description: Lowercase URL segment. Diacritics are stripped: husn-wa-qubh, not ḥusn-wa-qubḥ.

HoldingRef.description: A Position id (P_DCT), a position-as-held-by-a-thinker (P_DCT@al_Ashari), or — widened beyond research F.5 — a Question or Objection id. F.5 types both ends of an Equivalence as positions, but research B.2's third intersection relates Plato's Euthyphro *dilemma* to the ḥusn wa qubḥ *debate*: neither end is a position, and forcing them into position slots would have meant inventing two positions nobody holds. The loader resolves against positions first, then questions, then objections.

LocalizedString.description: A plain string is treated as English. i18n is first-class (research I.4): EN and TR. A missing locale renders the English with a visible 'not yet translated' mark — never a machine guess.

EpistemicStatus.description: Research epistemic legend. settled = uncontroversial among specialists; contested = live scholarly disagreement with sides named; uncertain = could not be established.

Side.description: One side of a scholarly dispute. Contested claims must surface the sides, not just the flag.

SourceRef.description: A link-and-cite reference to a reference work or secondary source. Per research E, SEP/IEP/PhilPapers text is never ingested; only cited. 'url' is only ever populated with a URL that has been verified to resolve.

perspectiveFlag.description: Research G.5: flag the confessional/sectarian slant of a source (e.g. 'al-Islam.org is Shi'i-inflected').

slug.description: URL segment. Stable and human-readable; ids are internal.

completeness.description: 'worked' = fully instantiated from the research. 'stub' = real structure, honest gaps.

refusesQuestion.description: true when the position does not answer the question but rejects its framing (research A.4). Drives the 'this tradition rejects the question' panel rather than an empty answer slot.

notYetWritten.description: Field names deliberately left empty. Renders as an honest empty state.

ScriptTerm.description: Research D. Store source script + fully diacriticized transliteration + the standard English rendering, separately. Display is diacritic-light by default with a user toggle.

translit.description: Fully diacriticized canonical form, e.g. 'ḥusn wa qubḥ'. The diacritic-light form is derived mechanically at render time, never stored.

searchAliases.description: Alternative spellings for identifier resolution. The canonical diacriticized name is often not what an authority file labels the person: Wikidata has 'Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari', not 'Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī'.

died.description: Free text so that hijri/CE double dates ('d. 324/936') survive.

wikidata.description: Research F.3: Wikidata Q-ID is the primary entity key. null means UNRESOLVED, never 'none'. Q-IDs are only ever written here after being resolved against wikidata.org — see scripts/resolve-wikidata.mjs.

coverageFlag.description: Research C coverage-thinness flag, surfaced in the UI so thin coverage is never mistaken for completeness.

HoldsRelation.description: Research F.2: a REIFIED relation, never a bare edge. This object is what lets the UI say 'Ockham — contested: denied by much recent scholarship' instead of flatly asserting the attribution.

targets.description: A Position id or an Argument id.

strongest.description: Marks the single best-attributed objection to the target — the one the confrontation step surfaces (research I.3b).

Equivalence.description: Research F.2/B.2. The cross-tradition intersection edge. This is the platform's distinctive surface and its highest-error surface, so evidence is required and the verdict is never a bare boolean.

partsWaysOn.description: Where the two part company. Never omitted for a 'genuine' verdict.

traditions.description: Explicit tradition pair, for intersections whose sides are not anchored to a thinker (and so cannot have their traditions derived from a holding).

transmissionLink.description: Whether any historical contact between the two is established. 'uncertain' for independent arrivals.

numbering.description: Canonical locator scheme: Bekker / Stephanus / Diels-Kranz / sura:aya / print pagination.

Passage.description: Every displayed quotation traces to one of these. 'text' is absent when the locus could not be verified (research Open Questions #4) — in that case attested MUST be false and the UI renders 'locus not verified' rather than a quotation.

locator.description: Bekker / Stephanus / sura:aya / chapter / print page.

url.description: A URL that was actually retrieved. Never constructed or recalled — scripts/verify-citations.mjs re-fetches every one.

linkOnly.description: The source is cited and linked but its text is deliberately not reproduced. SEP and IEP articles are licensed for linking and fair-use quotation, not redistribution (research E.1), so where they are the evidence for an attribution they appear as link-only passages rather than as quotations.

allOf.$comment: A passage with no text must say so explicitly rather than render an empty quotation.

Concept.description: Research D, the terminology equivalence map.

commonRendering.description: The standard English word, e.g. 'ethics' for akhlaq.

distortion.description: Where the standard English rendering distorts.

cluster.description: Concepts that must be shown as a unit (ren/yi/li).

surfaceForms.description: Exact strings that should be auto-glossed where they appear in body text. Authored rather than inferred: matching on the transliteration alone would gloss 'li' inside 'political' and miss 'ḥusn wa qubḥ' written diacritic-light. Matched whole-word, longest-first, first occurrence per block.

RealWorldCase.description: Research I.3d. An ordinary decision that the position bears on. Authored by the editors as a pedagogical scenario — never presented as a historical or textual claim.

editorial.description: Always true. Cases are editorial constructions and are labelled as such in the UI.

Tracer.description: Research I.3a: a commitment tracer, not a personality quiz. Each item is a proposition; each answer records what the answer ENTAILS and what it CONFLICTS WITH, so the result is a consistency report over Position nodes rather than a score.
